set.body:
Phase C.

kernel/AtomicFiles.scala:19-29 claims every write "forces its contents to stable storage". stageAndMove does force file contents (:213, channel.force(true)) but NEVER forces the containing directory after the rename (:218-224). On a crash, the rename itself can be lost even though the bytes were durable — so the documented guarantee is stronger than the implemented one.

Fix:
- Split the documented guarantee into THREE distinct claims: atomic visibility, single-publisher/no-replace, and crash durability. They have different implementations, different test strategies and different filesystem support.
- Either force the parent directory after rename, or narrow the wording to what is actually guaranteed. Decide per consumer — a journal and a result publisher may genuinely need different levels.
- Qualify network/shared-filesystem lock and rename semantics explicitly (NFS advisory locks and rename atomicity are not the local-filesystem story).
- Fail ACQUISITION when a consumer needs a guarantee that cannot be established on the target filesystem, rather than discovering it at write time.

Deliberately deferred: a public AtomicFsCapabilities ADT. Determine which consumers truly need each guarantee first; do not expose another premature abstraction. (Agrees with the review.)
set.title: P8.C2: Separate and qualify visibility, no-replace, and durability claims
